headline: Friday is the warmest day of the stretch, with highs around 80 at the coast and in the 80s inland, before a cooling trend leads into a strong Pacific storm Tuesday and Wednesday that is very likely to bring 1 inch or more of rain from the coast to the mountains, plus strong winds and possible thunderstorms.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: High pressure overhead keeps the warming going Friday, with highs 12 to 18 degrees above average from the coast to the coastal mountain slopes: around 80 near the coast and in the 80s in the valleys and inland coastal areas. The lower deserts also reach the 80s, and the mountains run from the lower 60s to lower 80s. Skies stay clear to partly cloudy, with high clouds moving in late Friday night.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Over the weekend the high pressure weakens and ocean breezes return and strengthen, so temperatures cool Saturday and Sunday while staying above average. By Sunday, highs at the coast and in the valleys are mostly in the 70s, around 80 in the lower deserts, and in the lower 50s to lower 70s in the mountains. Saturday morning's high clouds thin out Saturday afternoon into Sunday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Clouds increase Sunday night and Monday with a chance of showers late Sunday night and Monday, though the chance of a quarter inch or more of rain through Monday afternoon stays below 25 percent. Rain chances rise Monday night ahead of a strong Pacific storm on Tuesday, with the biggest impacts currently expected around Tuesday morning, bringing heavy rain, strong winds and a chance of thunderstorms. Through Wednesday night the chance of 1 inch or more of rain is above 90 percent from the coast to the mountains; the chance of 3 inches or more is 40 to 50 percent in far northern San Diego County (including the Carlsbad area) and 25 to 35 percent in far southern San Diego County, and in Orange and southwestern San Bernardino Counties it ranges from 35 to 45 percent near the coast to 60 to 70 percent in the mountains. Snow levels stay mostly above 8,000 feet through Tuesday, and rain continues Tuesday night into Wednesday before tapering off Wednesday night and Thursday as the storm moves farther inland and east.

coast: Friday's 10 AM high tide peaks around 7.6 to 7.7 feet, with tides running about a foot above normal predictions, so King Tides plus elevated surf bring moderate coastal flooding Friday morning under a Coastal Flood Warning for the Orange and San Diego County coasts until 1 PM Friday. A long-period west swell is still producing 4 to 6 foot breakers with local sets to 7 feet on exposed west-facing beaches; surf slowly eases but stays elevated through Saturday evening, with a Beach Hazards Statement from 1 PM Friday through Saturday afternoon. Saturday's high tide near 7 feet may bring minor coastal flooding Saturday morning, and high tides drop below 7 feet Sunday. No hazardous boating conditions are expected through Monday, but Tuesday's storm could bring gale-force winds over the coastal waters and high surf.
watch_for: Moderate coastal flooding around Friday's 10 AM King Tide, under a Coastal Flood Warning until 1 PM Friday
Timing and rain totals for the Tuesday–Wednesday storm, with a 40 to 50 percent chance of 3 inches or more in northern San Diego County
Strong winds and a chance of thunderstorms with that storm on Tuesday
confidence: Confidence is high in the warm, dry weather through the weekend and very high that the Tuesday–Wednesday storm brings at least an inch of rain, while its exact timing and whether totals reach 3 inches or more remain uncertain.
